articles.title: Supply shocks to weaken monetary policy effectiveness: CEA Nageswaran
articles.summary:
Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran on Friday said monetary policy tools such as interest rate adjustments may become less effective in tackling inflation in a world increasingly vulnerable to supply-side disruptions.
"Fiscal and other public policy measures will be more important because raising interest rates will not solve the supply-induced problems. If anything, it may even be counter-productive," he said at the 9th Annual Food Systems Dialogue here.
Amid persistent supply induced issues, countries will have to use all kinds of flexibilities with regards to the inflation targeting framework, he said.
"Since 2022, very few countries have met their inflation target. So, it will be there as a framework, but I think countries will take creative liberties with it, as they have to," he added.

articles.title: Sensex, Nifty's explosive rally pushes market to pre-Middle East war levels. How long will they take to scale fresh peaks?
articles.summary: The return of FIIs and easing oil prices sparked a skyrocketing rally in the Indian stock market this month, pushing the benchmark indices to levels not seen since the Middle East war ensued earlier this year, but analysts say it may take a few more months for them to hit fresh lifetime highs.Sensex this week touched 82,000, marking the first time since last February before US-Israel’s joint air strikes killed Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, beginning a conflict that sparked a sharp surge in oil prices and spooked investors, continuing till date. Nifty traded above 25,350 before the infamous March selloff began. The index has now traced its way back above the level.Also read |Sensex erases all Middle East war losses but is it too soon to forget the Hormuz factor?How far are Sensex, Nifty from their lifetime highs?Despite the recent gains, the benchmark indices are sharply down from their respective lifetime lows. Sensex had hit a lifetime high of 86,159 on December 1 last year, and Nifty had hit an all-time high of 26,373 early in January this year. The benchmark indices are around 5% away from their respective record peaks despite the recent rally.Sensex has recovered over 11,000 from its recent low to hover near 81,900, which leaves 86,000 about 5% away. Vaqarjaved Khan, Senior Fundamental analyst at Angel One, feels that this rally has fundamental support. Earnings visibility is improving, banking, autos and consumption are showing healthier demand, and softer input costs are helping margins, he said, adding that steady SIP flows from domestic investors also give the market a cushion even when foreign money turns cautious. Sensex’s recovery of over 11,000 points from its October low reflects a sharp improvement in market sentiment, supported by renewed foreign institutional inflows, easing crude oil prices and encouraging corporate earnings, said Vinit Bolinjkar, Head of Research, Ventura. Why caution is warranted after such sharp spikeHowever, after such a steep rally, some consolidation and profit booking cannot be ruled out, the analyst said. While the broader market outlook remains positive, geopolitical uncertainties, inflationary pressures and fluctuations in foreign capital flows could create intermittent volatility, according to Bolinjkar. “We expect the next leg of the rally to be increasingly driven by earnings growth rather than liquidity alone.”“I would not call valuations comfortable after such a sharp run. Earnings need to catch up with prices, and that is what I will be watching in the coming quarters. Crude oil, global cues and foreign inflows will decide how quickly we move,” Khan from Angel One said.The current rally has been driven by falling crude levels, the return of foreign money and better-than-expected earnings. All three need to hold, and none of them is guaranteed while the US-Iran situation remains unresolved and the Fed stays hawkish, said Tanvi Kanchan, Associate Director at Anand Rathi Shares & Stock Brokers. She noted that the market is already showing signs of fatigue near these levels as the Sensex has slipped back from its November 11 high and has been trading in a narrow range on Thursday.Also read | Rs 80,000 crore FII buying sparks explosive rally on Dalal Street. Will RBI rate hike worries kill the party?When could Sensex, Nifty soar back to lifetime highs?A fresh lifetime high, which is sustainable, is a realistic possibility over the next few months rather than the next few sessions, provided crude stays contained and foreign flows remain positive, one can expect short term consolidation before the breakout, according to Kanchan from Anand Rathi.Khan from Angel One has a base case that the Sensex can cross 86,000 and set a fresh lifetime high in roughly three to six months, provided Q3 FY27 earnings hold up and there is no external shock. “I would advise investors not to chase the rally and to accumulate quality large caps on dips.”Ventura analyst Vinit Bolinjkar believes that Sensex could test the 86,000–86,200 zone over the next two to three months, provided foreign inflows remain strong, crude prices stay contained and corporate earnings sustain their momentum. “A decisive breakout above the immediate resistance of 82,500 could pave the way towards 84,000 and eventually 86,000,” he said.Sudeep Shah, Head of Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities, said if the market succeeds in holding on to its bullish momentum, Sensex could potentially revisit its lifetime highs over the next 3-6 weeks. “However, investors should not expect the rally to be linear. After such a sharp recovery, intermittent profit-booking and consolidation would be healthy and could provide a stronger base for the next leg of the uptrend,” according to Shah.Ajit Mishra, SVP of Research at Religare Broking, meanwhile believe Sensex is well positioned to reclaim the 86,000 mark and potentially surpass its previous lifetime high over the next 3-6 months. However, the next leg of the rally will need earnings delivery rather than just valuation re-rating, he said, adding that investors should use intermittent corrections to accumulate fundamentally strong businesses with sustainable growth prospects.Also read |MSCI rejig: LIC, Meesho, Coforge set to gain from index inclusion. articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure on Thursday raised concerns not only about the future of the multitrillion-dollar chipmaker but also about its willingness and ability to continue financing the artificial intelligence boom, Reuters reported.Huang’s exit added another pressure point to one of the global market’s most crowded trades. It came after Nvidia’s board met late Wednesday to consider the longtime CEO’s future following reports of two extramarital affairs.Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while Nvidia searches for a permanent successor, the company said in a statement.Investors initially sold Nvidia shares and stocks linked to the company, including data-centre operator CoreWeave and South Korea’s Naver. Shares of chipmaking rivals Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices advanced.Chinese graphics-processing-unit makers also rallied on expectations that Nvidia’s leadership upheaval could help local suppliers gain market share. Moore Threads, MetaX and Cambricon each surged nearly 10%.Nvidia shares fell 13%, while Nasdaq 100 futures declined 0.6%.The broader concern is that Nvidia could scale back its strategy of financing data centres under new leadership, potentially slowing investment across the AI industry.Also Read | Anthropic IPO: Can Indian investors apply for Claude maker's $64 billion share sale? Check rules“Nvidia has been called the ‘Bank of AI’. They’ll sell you the chips and loan you the money. If they have to take a step back because of what’s going on, will that cut off funding to smaller companies that need it? That’s an open question,” said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading in Chatham, New Jersey, according to Reuters.Nvidia has been the flagship stock of the AI revolution. Its technological lead and surging sales have driven its share price up about 900% in the four years since the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT helped usher in the generative-AI era.The company has also emerged as a major financier of the industry, investing billions of dollars in customers through equity stakes and other financial commitments as it anticipates growing demand for increasingly powerful chips.“Nvidia’s credit support is what makes much of this debt finance-able across the AI hyperscaler deal front,” said Christopher Brown, senior vice president, investments, at Synovus Securities. “Lenders will ask what happens to that support if Nvidia’s leadership or regulatory standing is impaired, and Nvidia’s own willingness to extend more guarantees may be constrained.”Nvidia’s board launched an investigation into Huang after reports that he had an affair with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese spy. A separate report involving another alleged affair emerged before Wednesday’s board meeting.Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, told Reuters that Nvidia’s revenue was unlikely to fall suddenly following Huang’s departure. The greater concern, he said, was the company’s long-term direction because of Huang’s central role in shaping its computing strategy.“Replacing that strategic vision ... is an enormous challenge,” Boloor said.Nvidia’s departure reverberates across AI stocksHuang’s exit creates a leadership vacuum at the roughly $4 trillion company he co-founded and built over more than three decades. Nvidia has become the leading supplier of AI chips and a focal point of the technology rivalry between the United States and China.Asian chip stocks, which had rallied alongside Nvidia during the AI spending boom but recently came under pressure from concerns about financing costs and demand, also declined.Nvidia disclosed $164.5 billion in financial commitments in its latest earnings report. These included an obligation of up to $105 billion tied to an OpenAI data centre in Ohio and more than $50 billion in lease and capacity guarantees.In August, Nvidia said it had partnered with six major financial institutions, including Apollo, BlackRock and Blackstone, to establish computing-finance platforms seeking more than $500 billion in third-party capital for AI infrastructure. Huang said the company could backstop as much as $125 billion, or 25% of the potential deals.“The interlocking deals that Nvidia has with so much of the industry raise the question of whether that created more stability or more fragility,” Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers, told Reuters.Nvidia is also an investor in Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot. Anthropic’s initial public offering this month is expected to test investor demand for AI-related assets.CoreWeave shares fell more than 7.5% in premarket trading after surging Wednesday on upbeat earnings. Naver, in which Nvidia invested $1 billion by financing a data-centre expansion, dropped 6%.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. articles.title: What Nvidia said after CEO’s shocking exit
articles.summary: In a move that would certainly send shockwaves through the tech world, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the company as president, chief executive officer (CEO) and a member of the company's board of directors, with immediate effect on Thursday.Meanwhile, Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been appointed as interim chief executive officer as the chip giant begins a search for a permanent successor.Nvidia's board said it will consider both internal and external candidates for the position. Kress will continue to serve as the company's executive vice president and CFO while serving as interim CEO until a permanent successor is appointed.Also Read | Jensen Huang quits as Nvidia CEO amid affair scandal; AI chip giant names Colette Kress interim chiefThe company did not disclose a reason for Huang's resignation in its announcement.Kress has served as Nvidia's executive vice president and CFO since joining the company in September 2013. During her tenure, she has led the company's finance organisation and played a key role in Nvidia's growth and evolution.Before joining Nvidia, Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft.What Nvidia's board saidHarvey C. Jones, who has been appointed Nvidia's first-ever chair of the board, said Kress has helped lead the company through a period of “extraordinary growth” and has a deep understanding of its business, customers, operations and financial position.The board said it has “full confidence” in Kress and the leadership team and expects Nvidia's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.“NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” Kress said.She added that Nvidia would continue advancing its work in accelerated computing and AI while focusing on customers, partners, developers and shareholders.Also Read | Jensen Huang and the Chinese spy honeytrap: How does China allegedly use this strategy to gather sensitive US information?Jensen Huang's Nvidia legacyThe board said Huang's contributions to Nvidia were “profound” and described the company as one of the world's most consequential technology companies.“The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” Nvidia said.Huang founded Nvidia and has led the company for 33 years, overseeing its transformation into a dominant player in accelerated computing and AI.A private affair, a very public exitHuang, 63, co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has been at the helm of the company for more than three decades. During that time, he transformed Nvidia from a graphics chipmaker into one of the biggest beneficiaries of the global artificial intelligence boom. His departure marks a major change for the company and the semiconductor industry.Huang's exit comes amid a controversy involving Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, whom US intelligence agencies suspect of gathering information for Beijing. Huang admitted to having an extramarital relationship with her and apologised to his wife, children and Nvidia employees.The revelations prompted Nvidia's board to launch an independent investigation into reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The company, however, said its board had no reason to believe that US national security or Nvidia's confidential information had been compromised. The affair finally cost Huang to step down from his position from the company.

articles.title: Kimberly Powell: Nvidia career in spotlight
articles.summary: Kimberly Powell has spent 18 years at Nvidia, moving from medical imaging to some of the company's biggest healthcare AI projects, including genomics and drug discovery. But the 48-year-old vice president is now in the headlines for a different reason.The New York Times reported on November 11 that she had an intimate relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, 63, who is her direct boss. The report cited five people who worked at the company and said the two were seen being affectionate in a video recorded at a San Jose hotel during an Nvidia conference in March. Powell is married, the newspaper reported.When the Times asked Huang about his relationship with Powell, he reportedly replied, "I don't think you should be talking to me directly," before ending the call. Powell and Nvidia had not responded to Business Insider's requests for comment as of November 12. Neither has confirmed the reported relationship.The report comes as Nvidia is already dealing with another controversy involving Huang. The CEO recently told employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without naming anyone.Separately, the company's board has been examining whether a technology executive with alleged links to Chinese intelligence targeted Huang. That case involves Alice Huang, not Kimberly Powell. Together, the developments have put the company's leadership, internal policies and board oversight under fresh scrutiny.Who is Kimberly Powell and what is her role at Nvidia?Powell is one of Nvidia's senior executives responsible for taking its AI computing technology beyond conventional chip applications. Her current role covers healthcare and life sciences, two areas where Nvidia wants to expand the use of accelerated computing and artificial intelligence.        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Yahoo Finance (@yahoofinance)She joined Nvidia in 2008 as a director. Her initial responsibility was to establish Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) as computing accelerators for medical imaging equipment.Before joining Nvidia, Powell worked in hardware engineering and product management at Planar Systems, where she focused on diagnostic imaging systems. She holds a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, with a concentration in computer engineering, from Northeastern University.Her entry into Nvidia was not the result of a conventional executive recruitment process. On an August 2026 episode of the Lifers podcast, she explained that she had contacted Nvidia to discuss its computing technology. The company subsequently recognised its potential applications in healthcare and approached her about joining.She described the opportunity as a "dream come true."Powell's responsibilities grew over the years. Her LinkedIn profile says she became a senior director in 2016, leading an AI-focused business development team. In 2017, she was promoted to vice president of healthcare.When she joined in 2008, one of the main opportunities was using GPUs to process medical images. Medical imaging systems generate large volumes of data, and GPUs can process many calculations simultaneously. This makes them useful for applications such as analysing CT scans, MRI images and other diagnostic images.Over time, Nvidia expanded this approach into other parts of healthcare.Its medical imaging platform, MONAI, provides tools for developing AI applications that analyse medical images. Its BioNeMo platform supports AI research in biology and drug discovery. Parabricks uses accelerated computing to process genomic data.Powell's role has therefore expanded from promoting GPUs for imaging equipment to developing a wider computing and software ecosystem for healthcare companies, hospitals and pharmaceutical researchers.According to her profile on the Milken Institute's website, she also oversees the global strategy and commercial expansion of these platforms.Kimberly Powell report and Alice Huang investigationThe Powell report is the second major development involving Huang's personal relationships to emerge during Nvidia's current leadership crisis. But the two cases concern different women and different allegations.The first involves Alice Huang, a technology executive associated with Megaspeed. The New York Times previously reported that US officials believed she might have been recruited by the Chinese government to gather information about Nvidia.The allegations have raised national security questions because Nvidia makes some of the world's most advanced AI chips, which are subject to US export restrictions on sales to China.Nvidia's board launched an investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The company has also faced scrutiny over its relationship with Alice Huang and the circumstances surrounding the alleged intelligence operation.The issue has also reached Congress. Republican lawmakers have sought a closed-door briefing from Huang on his relationship with Alice Huang and the national security concerns surrounding Nvidia's business in China.On November 11, Reuters reported that Nvidia's board had met to consider whether Huang should be removed as CEO. The Wall Street Journal separately reported that the board was preparing to oust him.Nvidia has 11 board members, including Huang. Under the company's bylaws, a majority of directors can remove him, with or without cause. All directors other than Huang are considered independent.As of November 12, no final removal decision had been publicly announced.Reuters also reported that there was no obvious successor if Huang were removed. Nvidia's CFO Colette Kress and senior data-centre executive Ian Buck have been mentioned in discussions about possible leadership arrangements, but no successor has been announced.Nvidia is scheduled to report its quarterly results on November 17.Nvidia shares closed at $173.73 on November 11, gaining 2.87% during the regular session. However, the stock fell more than 8% in extended trading after reports that the board was considering Huang's future.Reuters reported that Nvidia shares also fell around 7% in early Frankfurt trading on November 12. The company's market value had declined by roughly $600 billion since the board announced its investigation into the Alice Huang matter, according to the report.

articles.title: Megaspeed pledges cooperation with US amid Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang scandal
articles.summary:
Megaspeed, the Singapore-headquartered tech company at the center of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's scandal, pledged Thursday to cooperate with investigations into concerns over risks to US national security.
In its first statement since Huang admitted to having an affair with a Chinese woman and former executive of the company, Megaspeed said Thursday that it takes its obligation to comply with US export control laws "extremely seriously."
"Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government."
Nvidia's board of directors was reported to be meeting to discuss Huang's situation but there was no word on any outcome from those discussions.
